dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:5101.text: Middle. Formed from 人, with 田 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “Ride the middle 佃,” a single-shaft carriage.

shuowen:5102.text: A small appearance. Formed from 人, with 囟 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Small indeed is that house.”

shuowen:5103.text: A small appearance. Formed from 人, with 光 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Discourses of the States says: “Small meals do not equal one proper meal.”

shuowen:5104.text: Frivolous, careless or lacking seriousness. Formed from 人, with 兆 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “He does not treat the people frivolously.”

shuowen:5105.text: To avoid. Formed from 人, with 辟 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “As if bending to the left.” Another explanation: pulling from the side.

shuowen:5106.text: Obstinate. Formed from 人, with abbreviated 弦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5107.text: To associate or join. Formed from 人, with 支 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The harmful man joins in wrongdoing.”

shuowen:5108.text: To cover the sides of the body. Formed from 人, with 多 indicating the sound. Another explanation: extravagant.

shuowen:5109.text: A foolish appearance. Formed from 人, with 台 indicating the sound. Read like 騃.

shuowen:5110.text: Proud or arrogant. Formed from 人, with 蚤 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5111.text: Deceitful. Formed from 人, with 爲 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5112.text: Idle or slack. Formed from 人, with 只 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5113.text: To attend to business, 務. Formed from 人, with 句 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5114.text: Light or frivolous. Formed from 人, with 㶾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5115.text: Music or entertainment. Formed from 人, with 昌 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5116.text: Play or performance. Formed from 人, with 非 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5117.text: To assume a pose. Formed from 人, with 善 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5118.text: 儳互, uneven or irregular. Formed from 人, with 毚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5119.text: A person withdrawn from public life. Formed from 人, with 失 indicating the sound. Another explanation: careless or neglectful.

shuowen:5120.text: To walk leaning. Formed from 人, with 我 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The slanting cap tilts.”

shuowen:5121.text: Joyful. Formed from 人, with 䚻 indicating the sound. West of the passes, things differing in size are called 㑾.

shuowen:5122.text: 徼𠊬, to suffer constraint or wrong. Formed from 人, with 卻 indicating the sound; the precise expression is uncertain.

shuowen:5123.text: The appearance of drunken dancing. Formed from 人, with 差 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Repeatedly dancing, swaying drunkenly.”

shuowen:5124.text: The appearance of drunken dancing. Formed from 人, with 欺 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Repeatedly dancing, staggering.”

shuowen:5125.text: To injure. Formed from 人, with 𣫭 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5126.text: Jealous. Formed from 人, with 疾 indicating the sound. Another explanation: poisonous or harmful.

shuowen:5127.text: Light or disrespectful. Formed from 人, with 易 indicating the sound. Another explanation: exchanging with one another, 交㑥.

shuowen:5128.text: To face one another in litigation, each claiming to be right. Formed from 人, with 希 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5129.text: To fall prostrate. Formed from 人, with 賁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5130.text: To fall prostrate. Formed from 人, with 畺 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5131.text: To fall down. Formed from 人, with 卜 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5132.text: To lie prostrate. Formed from 人, with 匽 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5133.text: A wound. Formed from 人, with abbreviated 𥏻 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5134.text: To stab. Formed from 人, with 肴 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a cry of pain.

shuowen:5135.text: An expression of displeasure, 𢞎. Formed from 人, with 夸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5136.text: To match or accompany one another, 相儔. Formed from 人, with 崔 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The household members all press upon me.”

shuowen:5137.text: Pain. Formed from 人, with 甬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5138.text: To watch or oversee. Formed from 人 and 犬.

shuowen:5139.text: To press or constrain. Formed from 人, with 足 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5140.text: To compare or align. Formed from 人, with 𠛱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5141.text: To bind together. Formed from 人 and 系; 系 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:5142.text: To strike. Formed from a person holding 戈. Another explanation: to defeat.

shuowen:5143.text: What an army captures. Formed from 人, with 孚 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “Take them as captives and severed ears.”

shuowen:5144.text: To bare the upper body. Formed from 人, with 旦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5145.text: Bent or stooping. Formed from 人, with 區 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5146.text: Crooked or deformed. Formed from 人, with 婁 indicating the sound. The text says the Duke of Zhou was 韈僂; some explain this as a bent back. The phrase 韈僂 is uncertain.

shuowen:5147.text: A foolish manner of walking, 僇僇. Formed from 人, with 翏 indicating the sound. Read like 雡. Another explanation: for the time being, 且.

shuowen:5148.text: An adversary. Formed from 人, with 九 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5149.text: To defeat or damage one another. Formed from 人, with 畾 indicating the sound. Read like 雷.

shuowen:5150.text: Disaster. Formed from 人 and 各; 各 means opposing one another.

shuowen:5151.text: To separate. Formed from 人, with 比 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “There is a woman, parted and separated.”

shuowen:5152.text: To destroy or disparage. Formed from 人, with 咎 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5153.text: 仳倠, an ugly face. Formed from 人, with 隹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5154.text: To place. Formed from 人, with 直 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5155.text: To entrust. Formed from 人, with 㡯 indicating the sound; 㡯 is ancient-script 宅.

shuowen:5156.text: To gather. Formed from 人, with 尊 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Gathering and crowding, hating behind the back” (僔沓背僧); the recorded wording is uncertain.

shuowen:5157.text: To resemble or be an image. Formed from 人 and 象; 象 also indicates the sound. Read like 養.

shuowen:5158.text: Weary. Formed from 人, with 卷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5159.text: To end. Formed from 人, with 曹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5160.text: A human figure made of paulownia wood. Formed from 人, with 禺 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5161.text: To inquire after the dead. Ancient burials covered the body thickly with firewood. Formed from a person holding a bow, assembled to drive away birds.

shuowen:5162.text: The 佋 and 穆 ranks in a temple: the father is 佋, facing south; the son 穆, facing north. Formed from 人, with 召 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5163.text: A spirit. Formed from 人, with 身 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5164.text: To live long and depart as an immortal. Formed from 人 and 䙴; 䙴 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:5165.text: A Man or Yi people of Jianwei. Formed from 人, with 棘 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5166.text: A person on a mountain. Formed from 人 and 山.

shuowen:5167.text: In the south are the Jiaoyao people, three chi tall, the utmost in shortness. Formed from 人, with 堯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5168.text: To go all around. Formed from 人, with 對 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5169.text: To travel far. Formed from 人, with 狂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5170.text: To divide. Formed from 人 and 牛; an ox is a large thing and can therefore be divided.

shuowen:5171.text: A companion. Formed from 人, with 呂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5172.text: A young boy. Formed from 人, with 辰 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5173.text: A deputy or second. Formed from 人, with 卒 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5174.text: To follow or attend. Formed from 人, with 兼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5175.text: 倜儻, unrestrained. Formed from 人 and 周. Further details are unknown.

shuowen:5176.text: Unrestrained, 倜儻. Formed from 人, with 黨 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5177.text: The rows of dancers. Formed from 人, with 䏌 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5178.text: To fall. Formed from 人, with 到 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5179.text: To bring together a market transaction. Formed from 人 and 會; 會 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:5180.text: Low. Formed from 人 and 氐; 氐 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:5181.text: A debt owed. Formed from 人 and 責; 責 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:5182.text: The value of a thing. Formed from 人 and 賈; 賈 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:5183.text: To stop. Formed from 人, with 亭 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5184.text: To hire. Formed from 人 and 就; 就 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:5185.text: To watch and wait. Formed from 人, with 司 indicating the sound. The six characters from 低 onward, all formed from 人, were added by later people.

shuowen:5186.text: A Buddhist religious practitioner. Formed from 人, with 曾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5187.text: To stand for a long time. Formed from 人 and 宁.

shuowen:5188.text: To inquire. Formed from 人, with 貞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5189.text: To change. Formed from inverted 人. All characters in this group are formed from 𠤎.

shuowen:5190.text: Not yet settled. Formed from 𠤎, with 𥎨 indicating the sound; 𥎨 is ancient-script 矢.

shuowen:5191.text: An immortal changing form and ascending to Heaven. Formed from 𠤎, 目 and 乚, pronounced 隱; 八 is what carries the immortal.

shuowen:5192.text: Teaching put into practice. Formed from 𠤎 and 人; 𠤎 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:5193.text: To compare and arrange with one another. Formed from reversed 人. 匕 is also used to take food by close scooping; another name is 柶. All characters in this group are formed from 匕.

shuowen:5194.text: A spoon. Formed from 匕, with 是 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5195.text: To follow in succession. Formed from 匕 and 十. 鴇 follows this element.

shuowen:5196.text: To incline. Formed from 匕, with 支 indicating the sound; 匕 represents an inclined head. The Odes says: “Inclining is that Weaving Maid.”

shuowen:5197.text: A head not upright. Formed from 匕 and 頁.

shuowen:5198.text: The brain or marrow of the head. Formed from 匕, representing close attachment; 巛 depicts hair, 囟 the shape of the brain.

shuowen:5199.text: To look upward, wishing to approach or reach something. Formed from 匕 and 卪. The Odes says: “I look up to the high mountain.”

shuowen:5200.text: High. 早 with 匕 makes 㔬; 匕 with 卪 makes 卬. They all have the same meaning.
